newsitem.title: GERMANY: Situation in flood-hit east Germany still serious.
newsitem.headline: Situation in flood-hit east Germany still serious.

text.p: Officials said on Thursday the situation in flood-hit eastern Germany remained serious although new high water levels did not hit the region overnight as feared.
A spokesman for the interior ministry in the state of Brandenburg said water levels were rising slightly again and experts expected a new high point to be reached around midnight.
Government ministers paid visits to region, where around 5,000 people have already been ordered to leave their homes.
Defence Minister Volker Ruehe said 8,300 soldiers would be in place by the evening, carrying out the biggest non-military operation in the German army's postwar history.
Interior Minister Manfred Kanther said officials would also be looking to see if lessons could be learned from the preparations for the arrival of the floods.
"We'll document very carefully what could be done better in the future," he told reporters during his visit.
The first dyke on the Oder river burst on Wednesday south of Frankfurt. The interior ministry spokesman said water was now pouring through a 300-metre wide hole in the dyke.
But workers had been able to shore up another dyke near the town of Eisenhuettenstadt, he said, and no further evacuations were planned for the moment.
